payload_windows/aarch64/exec.description:
Executes an arbitrary command on a Windows on ARM (AArch64) target.
          This payload is a foundational example of position-independent shellcode for the AArch64 architecture.
          It dynamically resolves the address of the `WinExec` function from `kernel32.dll` by parsing the
          Process Environment Block (PEB) and the module's Export Address Table (EAT) at runtime.
          This technique avoids static imports and hardcoded function addresses, increasing resilience.

payload_windows/dns_txt_query_exec.description:
Performs a TXT query against a series of DNS record(s) and executes the returned x86 shellcode. The DNSZONE
          option is used as the base name to iterate over. The payload will first request the TXT contents of the a
          hostname, followed by b, then c, etc. until there are no more records. For each record that is returned, exactly
          255 bytes from it are copied into a buffer that is eventually executed. This buffer should be encoded using
          x86/alpha_mixed with the BufferRegister option set to EDI.
payload_windows/dns_txt_query_exec.name: DNS TXT Record Payload Download and Execution

payload_windows/format_all_drives.description:
This payload formats all mounted disks in Windows (aka ShellcodeOfDeath).

          After formatting, this payload sets the volume label to the string specified in
          the VOLUMELABEL option. If the code is unable to access a drive for any reason,
          it skips the drive and proceeds to the next volume.

          creates pcap files in /tmp with predictable file names. This exploits this by hard-linking these
          filenames to /etc/passwd, then sending a packet with a privileged user entry contained within.
          This, and all the other packets, are appended to /etc/passwd.

          Successful exploitation results in the creation of a new superuser account.

          This module requires manual clean-up. Upon success, you should remove /tmp/msf3-session*pcap
          files and truncate /etc/passwd. Note that if this module fails, you can potentially induce
          a permanent DoS on the target by corrupting the /etc/passwd file.

post_multi/gather/firefox_creds.description:
This module will collect credentials from the Firefox web browser if it is
          installed on the targeted machine. Additionally, cookies are downloaded. Which
          could potentially yield valid web sessions.

          Firefox stores passwords within the signons.sqlite database file. There is also a
          keys3.db file which contains the key for decrypting these passwords. In cases where
          a Master Password has not been set, the passwords can easily be decrypted using
          3rd party tools or by setting the DECRYPT option to true. Using the latter often
          needs root privileges. Also be warned that if your session dies in the middle of the
          file renaming process, this could leave Firefox in a non working state. If a
          Master Password was used the only option would be to bruteforce.

          Useful 3rd party tools:
          + firefox_decrypt (https://github.com/Unode/firefox_decrypt)
          + pswRecovery4Moz (https://github.com/philsmd/pswRecovery4Moz)

          as SYSTEM, the MIGRATE option must be enabled and the CAPTURE_TYPE option should be set to one of
          Explorer, Winlogon, or a specific PID. To capture the keystrokes of the interactive user, the
          Explorer option should be used with MIGRATE enabled. Keep in mind that this will demote this session

          option will capture the username and password entered into the logon and unlock dialog. The LOCKSCREEN
          option can be combined with the Winlogon CAPTURE_TYPE to for the user to enter their clear-text
          password. It is recommended to run this module as a job, otherwise it will tie up your framework user interface.

post_windows/gather/enum_ad_computers.name: Windows Gather Active Directory Computers

author: Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_groups.description: This module will enumerate AD groups on the specified domain.
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_groups.name: Windows Gather Active Directory Groups

author: Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_managedby_gr.description:
This module will enumerate AD groups on the specified domain which are specifically managed.
          It cannot at the moment identify whether the 'Manager can update membership list' option
          option set; if so, it would allow that member to update the contents of that group. This
          could either be used as a persistence mechanism (for example, set your user as the 'Domain
          Admins' group manager) or could be used to detect privilege escalation opportunities
          without having domain admin privileges.
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_managedby_gr.name: Windows Gather Active Directory Managed Groups

author: Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
Scott Sutherland
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_service_prin.description:
This module will enumerate servicePrincipalName in the default AD directory
          where the user is a member of the Domain Admins group.
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_service_prin.name: Windows Gather Active Directory Service Principal Names

author: Thomas Ring
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_to_wordlist.description:
This module will gather information from the default Active Domain (AD) directory
          and use these words to seed a wordlist. By default it enumerates user accounts to
          build the wordlist.
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_to_wordlist.name: Windows Active Directory Wordlist Builder

author: Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_user_comment.description:
This module will enumerate user accounts in the default Active Domain (AD) directory which
          contain 'pass' in their description or comment (case-insensitive) by default. In some cases,
          such users have their passwords specified in these fields.
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_user_comment.name: Windows Gather Active Directory User Comments

author: Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_users.description:
This module will enumerate user accounts in the default Active Domain (AD) directory and stores
          them in the database. If GROUP_MEMBER is set to the DN of a group, this will list the members of
          that group by performing a recursive/nested search (i.e. it will list users who are members of
          groups that are members of groups that are members of groups (etc) which eventually include the
          target group DN.
post_windows/gather/enum_ad_users.name: Windows Gather Active Directory Users

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_applications.description: This module will enumerate all installed applications on a Windows system
post_windows/gather/enum_applications.name: Windows Gather Installed Application Enumeration

author: averagesecurityguy <stephen@averagesecurityguy.info>
post_windows/gather/enum_artifacts.description:
This module will check the file system and registry for particular artifacts.

          The list of artifacts is read in YAML format from data/post/enum_artifacts_list.txt
          or a user specified file. Any matches are written to the loot.
post_windows/gather/enum_artifacts.name: Windows Gather File and Registry Artifacts Enumeration

author: rageltman <rageltman@sempervictus>
post_windows/gather/enum_av.description: This module will enumerate the AV products detected by WMIC
post_windows/gather/enum_av.name: Windows Installed AntiVirus Enumeration

author: Andrew Smith
Jon Hart <jon_hart@rapid7.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_av_excluded.description:
This module will enumerate the file, directory, process and
          extension-based exclusions from supported AV products, which
          currently includes Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Security
          Essentials/Antimalware, and Symantec Endpoint Protection.
post_windows/gather/enum_av_excluded.name: Windows Antivirus Exclusions Enumeration

author: Alexander "xaitax" Hagenah
post_windows/gather/enum_browsers.description:
This post-exploitation module extracts sensitive browser data from both Chromium-based and Gecko-based browsers
          on the target system. It supports the decryption of passwords and cookies using Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI)
          and can extract additional data such as browsing history, keyword search history, download history, autofill data,
          credit card information, browser cache and installed extensions.
post_windows/gather/enum_browsers.name: Advanced Browser Data Extraction for Chromium and Gecko Browsers

author: Nick Cottrell <ncottrellweb@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_chocolatey_appl.description: This module will enumerate all installed applications on a Windows system with chocolatey installed
post_windows/gather/enum_chocolatey_appl.name: Windows Gather Installed Application Within Chocolatey Enumeration

author: Sven Taute
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
Kx499
mubix <mubix@hak5.org>
post_windows/gather/enum_chrome.description:
This module will collect user data from Google Chrome and attempt to decrypt
          sensitive information.
post_windows/gather/enum_chrome.name: Windows Gather Google Chrome User Data Enumeration

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_computers.description: This module will enumerate computers included in the primary Active Directory domain.
post_windows/gather/enum_computers.name: Windows Gather Enumerate Computers

author: Barry Shteiman <barry@sectorix.com>
juan vazquez <juan.vazquez@metasploit.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_db.description: This module will enumerate a Windows system for installed database instances.
post_windows/gather/enum_db.name: Windows Gather Database Instance Enumeration

author: Brandon Perry <bperry.volatile@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_devices.description:
Enumerate PCI hardware information from the registry. Please note this script
          will run through registry subkeys such as: 'PCI', 'ACPI', 'ACPI_HAL', 'FDC', 'HID',
          'HTREE', 'IDE', 'ISAPNP', 'LEGACY'', LPTENUM', 'PCIIDE', 'SCSI', 'STORAGE', 'SW',
          and 'USB'; it will take time to finish. It is recommended to run this module as a
          background job.
post_windows/gather/enum_devices.name: Windows Gather Hardware Enumeration

author: Kx499
Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_dirperms.description:
This module enumerates directories and lists the permissions set
          on found directories. Please note: if the PATH option isn't specified,
          then the module will start enumerate whatever is in the target machine's
          %PATH% variable.
post_windows/gather/enum_dirperms.name: Windows Gather Directory Permissions Enumeration

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_domain.description:
This module identifies the primary Active Directory domain name
          and domain controller.
post_windows/gather/enum_domain.name: Windows Gather Enumerate Domain

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
Stephen Haywood <haywoodsb@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_domain_group_us.description:
This module extracts user accounts from the specified domain group
          and stores the results in the loot. It will also verify if session
          account is in the group. Data is stored in loot in a format that
          is compatible with the token_hunter plugin. This module must be
          run on a session running as a domain user.
post_windows/gather/enum_domain_group_us.name: Windows Gather Enumerate Domain Group

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_domain_tokens.description:
This module enumerates domain account tokens, processes running under
          domain accounts, and domain users in the local Administrators, Users
          and Backup Operator groups.
post_windows/gather/enum_domain_tokens.name: Windows Gather Enumerate Domain Tokens

author: Etienne Stalmans <etienne@sensepost.com>
Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
post_windows/gather/enum_domain_users.description:
This module will enumerate computers included in the primary Domain and attempt
          to list all locations the targeted user has sessions on. If the HOST option is specified
          the module will target only that host. If the HOST is specified and USER is set to nil, all users
          logged into that host will be returned.'
post_windows/gather/enum_domain_users.name: Windows Gather Enumerate Active Domain Users

author: mubix <mubix@hak5.org>
post_windows/gather/enum_domains.description:
This module enumerates currently the domains a host can see and the domain
          controllers for each domain.
post_windows/gather/enum_domains.name: Windows Gather Domain Enumeration

author: vysec <vincent.yiu@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_emet.description: This module will enumerate the EMET protected paths on the target host.
post_windows/gather/enum_emet.name: Windows Gather EMET Protected Paths

author: 3vi1john <Jbabio@me.com>
RageLtMan <rageltman@sempervictus>
post_windows/gather/enum_files.description: This module downloads files recursively based on the FILE_GLOBS option.
post_windows/gather/enum_files.name: Windows Gather Generic File Collection

author: vt <nick.freeman@security-assessment.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_hostfile.description: This module returns a list of entries in the target system's hosts file.
post_windows/gather/enum_hostfile.name: Windows Gather Windows Host File Enumeration

author: gwillcox-r7
post_windows/gather/enum_hyperv_vms.description:
This module will check if the target machine is a Hyper-V host and, if it is, will return a list of all
          of the VMs running on the host, as well as stats such as their state, version, CPU Usage, uptime, and status.
post_windows/gather/enum_hyperv_vms.name: Windows Hyper-V VM Enumeration

author: Kx499
post_windows/gather/enum_ie.description:
This module will collect history, cookies, and credentials (from either HTTP
          auth passwords, or saved form passwords found in auto-complete) in
          Internet Explorer. The ability to gather credentials is only supported
          for versions of IE >=7, while history and cookies can be extracted for all
          versions.
post_windows/gather/enum_ie.name: Windows Gather Internet Explorer User Data Enumeration

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_logged_on_users.description: This module will enumerate current and recently logged on Windows users.
post_windows/gather/enum_logged_on_users.name: Windows Gather Logged On User Enumeration (Registry)

author: Brandon Perry <bperry.volatile@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_ms_product_keys.description: This module will enumerate Microsoft product license keys.
post_windows/gather/enum_ms_product_keys.name: Windows Gather Product Key

author: TJ Glad <tjglad@cmail.nu>
post_windows/gather/enum_muicache.description:
This module gathers information about the files and file paths that logged on users have
          executed on the system. It also will check if the file still exists on the system. This
          information is gathered by using information stored under the MUICache registry key. If
          the user is logged in when the module is executed it will collect the MUICache entries
          by accessing the registry directly. If the user is not logged in the module will download
          users registry hive NTUSER.DAT/UsrClass.dat from the system and the MUICache contents are
          parsed from the downloaded hive.
post_windows/gather/enum_muicache.name: Windows Gather Enum User MUICache

author: Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_onedrive.description:
This module will identify the Office 365 OneDrive endpoints for both business and personal accounts
          across all users (providing access is permitted). It is useful for identifying document libraries
          that may otherwise not be obvious which could contain sensitive or useful information.
post_windows/gather/enum_onedrive.name: OneDrive Sync Provider Enumeration Module

author: zeroSteiner <zeroSteiner@gmail.com>
mubix <mubix@hak5.org>
post_windows/gather/enum_patches.description:
This module enumerates patches applied to a Windows system using the
          WMI query: SELECT HotFixID, InstalledOn FROM Win32_QuickFixEngineering.
post_windows/gather/enum_patches.name: Windows Gather Applied Patches

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_powershell_env.description: This module will enumerate Microsoft PowerShell settings.
post_windows/gather/enum_powershell_env.name: Windows Gather PowerShell Environment Setting Enumeration

author: TJ Glad <tjglad@cmail.nu>
post_windows/gather/enum_prefetch.description:
This module gathers prefetch file information from WinXP, Win2k3 and Win7 systems
          and current values of related registry keys. From each prefetch file we'll collect
          filetime (converted to utc) of the last execution, file path hash, run count, filename
          and the execution path.
post_windows/gather/enum_prefetch.name: Windows Gather Prefetch File Information

author: mubix <mubix@hak5.org>
post_windows/gather/enum_proxy.description:
This module pulls a user's proxy settings. If neither RHOST or SID
        are set it pulls the current user, else it will pull the user's settings
        for the specified SID and target host.
post_windows/gather/enum_proxy.name: Windows Gather Proxy Setting

author: Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_putty_saved_ses.description:
This module will identify whether Pageant (PuTTY Agent) is running and obtain saved session
          information from the registry. PuTTY is very configurable; some users may have configured
          saved sessions which could include a username, private key file to use when authenticating,
          host name etc.  If a private key is configured, an attempt will be made to download and store
          it in loot. It will also record the SSH host keys which have been stored. These will be connections that
          the user has previously after accepting the host SSH fingerprint and therefore are of particular
          interest if they are within scope of a penetration test.
post_windows/gather/enum_putty_saved_ses.name: PuTTY Saved Sessions Enumeration Module

author: Keith Faber
Kx499
post_windows/gather/enum_services.description:
This module will query the system for services and display name and
          configuration info for each returned service. It allows you to
          optionally search the credentials, path, or start type for a string
          and only return the results that match. These query operations are
          cumulative and if no query strings are specified, it just returns all
          services.  NOTE: If the script hangs, windows firewall is most likely
          on and you did not migrate to a safe process (explorer.exe for
          example).
post_windows/gather/enum_services.name: Windows Gather Service Info Enumeration

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_shares.description: This module will enumerate configured and recently used file shares.
post_windows/gather/enum_shares.name: Windows Gather SMB Share Enumeration via Registry

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
Tebo <tebo@attackresearch.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_snmp.description: This module will enumerate the SNMP service configuration.
post_windows/gather/enum_snmp.name: Windows Gather SNMP Settings

author: mubix <mubix@hak5.org>
post_windows/gather/enum_termserv.description: This module dumps MRU and connection data for RDP sessions.
post_windows/gather/enum_termserv.name: Windows Gather Terminal Server Client Connection Information Dumper

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_tokens.description:
This module enumerates Domain Admin account processes and delegation tokens.

          This module will first check if the session has sufficient privileges
          to replace process level tokens and adjust process quotas.

          The SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege privilege will not be assigned if
          the session has been elevated to SYSTEM. In that case try first
          migrating to another process that is running as SYSTEM.
post_windows/gather/enum_tokens.name: Windows Gather Enumerate Domain Admin Tokens (Token Hunter)

author: Barry Shteiman <barry@sectorix.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_tomcat.description:
This module will collect information from a Windows-based Apache Tomcat. You will get
          information such as: The installation path, Tomcat version, port, web applications,
          users, passwords, roles, etc.
post_windows/gather/enum_tomcat.name: Windows Gather Apache Tomcat Enumeration

author: vysec <vincent.yiu@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/enum_trusted_locatio.description: This module will enumerate the Microsoft Office trusted locations on the target host.
post_windows/gather/enum_trusted_locatio.name: Windows Gather Microsoft Office Trusted Locations

author: Sean Verity <veritysr1980@gmail.com>
sinn3r <sinn3r@metasploit.com>
Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
GhostlyBox
post_windows/gather/enum_unattend.description:
This module will check the file system for a copy of unattend.xml and/or
          autounattend.xml found in Windows Vista, or newer Windows systems.  And then
          extract sensitive information such as usernames and decoded passwords.  Also
          checks for '.vmimport' files that could have been created by the AWS EC2 VMIE service.
post_windows/gather/enum_unattend.name: Windows Gather Unattended Answer File Enumeration

actions.description: Export and download a chosen mailbox in the form of a .PST file, with support for an optional filter keyword
actions.name: EXPORT

actions.description: List basic information about all Exchange servers and mailboxes hosted on the target
actions.name: LIST

author: SophosLabs Offensive Security team
post_windows/gather/exchange.description:
This module will gather information from an on-premise Exchange Server running on the target machine.

          Two actions are supported:
          LIST (default action): List basic information about all Exchange servers and mailboxes hosted on the target.
          EXPORT: Export and download a chosen mailbox in the form of a .PST file, with support for an optional filter keyword.

          For a list of valid filters, see https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/filterable-properties-for-the-contentfilter-parameter

          The executing user has to be assigned to the "Organization Management" role group for the module to successfully run.

          Tested on Exchange Server 2010 on Windows Server 2012 R2 and Exchange Server 2016 on Windows Server 2016.
post_windows/gather/exchange.name: Windows Gather Exchange Server Mailboxes

author: Danil Bazin <danil.bazin@hsc.fr>
post_windows/gather/file_from_raw_ntfs.description:
This module gathers a file using the raw NTFS device, bypassing some Windows restrictions
          such as open file with write lock. Because it avoids the usual file locking issues, it can
          be used to retrieve files such as NTDS.dit.
post_windows/gather/file_from_raw_ntfs.name: Windows File Gather File from Raw NTFS

author: Joshua Harper <josh@radixtx.com>
post_windows/gather/forensics/browser_hi.description: Gathers Skype chat logs, Firefox history, and Chrome history data from the target machine.
post_windows/gather/forensics/browser_hi.name: Windows Gather Skype, Firefox, and Chrome Artifacts

author: Marcus J. Carey <mjc@threatagent.com>
post_windows/gather/forensics/duqu_check.description: This module searches for CVE-2011-3402 (Duqu) related registry artifacts.
post_windows/gather/forensics/duqu_check.name: Windows Gather Forensics Duqu Registry Check

author: Wesley McGrew <wesley@mcgrewsecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/forensics/enum_drive.description: This module will list physical drives and logical volumes
post_windows/gather/forensics/enum_drive.name: Windows Gather Physical Drives and Logical Volumes

author: William M.
post_windows/gather/forensics/fanny_bmp_.description:
This module searches for the Fanny.bmp worm related reg keys.
          fannybmp is a worm that exploited zero day vulns
          (more specifically, the LNK Exploit CVE-2010-2568).
          Which allowed it to spread even if USB Autorun was turned off.
          This is the same exploit that was used in StuxNet.
post_windows/gather/forensics/fanny_bmp_.name: FannyBMP or DementiaWheel Detection Registry Check

author: Wesley McGrew <wesley@mcgrewsecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/forensics/imager.description: This module will perform byte-for-byte imaging of remote disks and volumes.
post_windows/gather/forensics/imager.name: Windows Gather Forensic Imaging

author: Wesley McGrew <wesley@mcgrewsecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/forensics/nbd_server.description:
Maps remote disks and logical volumes to a local Network Block Device server.
          Allows for forensic tools to be executed on the remote disk directly.
post_windows/gather/forensics/nbd_server.name: Windows Gather Local NBD Server

author: Borja Merino <bmerinofe@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/forensics/recovery_f.description:
This module lists and attempts to recover deleted files from NTFS file systems. Use
          the FILES option to guide recovery. Leave this option empty to enumerate deleted files in the
          DRIVE. Set FILES to an extension (e.g., "pdf") to recover deleted files with that
          extension, or set FILES to a comma separated list of IDs (from enumeration) to
          recover those files. The user must have account file enumeration. Recovery
          may take a long time; use the TIMEOUT option to abort enumeration or recovery by
          extension after a specified period (in seconds).
post_windows/gather/forensics/recovery_f.name: Windows Gather Deleted Files Enumeration and Recovering

author: jerrelgordon
post_windows/gather/get_bookmarks.description: This module discovers information about a target by retrieving their bookmarked websites on Google Chrome, Opera and Microsoft Edge.
post_windows/gather/get_bookmarks.name: Bookmarked Sites Retriever

author: hdm <x@hdm.io>
post_windows/gather/hashdump.description: This module will dump the local user accounts from the SAM database using the registry
post_windows/gather/hashdump.name: Windows Gather Local User Account Password Hashes (Registry)

author: Brandon McCann "zeknox" <bmccann@accuvant.com>
Thomas McCarthy "smilingraccoon" <smilingraccoon@gmail.com>
Royce Davis "r3dy" <rdavis@accuvant.com>
post_windows/gather/local_admin_search_e.description:
This module will identify systems in a given range that the
          supplied domain user (should migrate into a user pid) has administrative
          access to by using the Windows API OpenSCManagerA to establishing a handle
          to the remote host. Additionally it can enumerate logged in users and group
          membership via Windows API NetWkstaUserEnum and NetUserGetGroups.
post_windows/gather/local_admin_search_e.name: Windows Gather Local Admin Search

author: Rob Bathurst <rob.bathurst@foundstone.com>
post_windows/gather/lsa_secrets.description:
This module will attempt to enumerate the LSA Secrets keys within the registry. The registry value used is:
          HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Security\Policy\Secrets\. Thanks goes to Maurizio Agazzini and Mubix for decrypt
          code from cachedump.
post_windows/gather/lsa_secrets.name: Windows Enumerate LSA Secrets

author: Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/make_csv_orgchart.description:
This module will generate a CSV file containing all users and their managers, which can be
          imported into Visio which will render it.
post_windows/gather/make_csv_orgchart.name: Generate CSV Organizational Chart Data Using Manager Information

author: smashery
post_windows/gather/memory_dump.description:
This module creates a memory dump of a process (to disk) and downloads the file
          for offline analysis.

          Options for DUMP_TYPE affect the completeness of the dump:

          "full" retrieves the entire process address space (all allocated pages);
          "standard" excludes image files (e.g. DLLs and EXEs in the address space) as
          well as memory mapped files. As a result, this option can be significantly
          smaller in size.
post_windows/gather/memory_dump.name: Windows Process Memory Dump

author: bannedit <bannedit@metasploit.com>
post_windows/gather/memory_grep.description:
This module allows for searching the memory space of a process for potentially
          sensitive data.  Please note: When the HEAP option is enabled, the module will have
          to migrate to the process you are grepping, and will not migrate back automatically.
          This means that if the user terminates the application after using this module, you
          may lose your session.
post_windows/gather/memory_grep.name: Windows Gather Process Memory Grep

author: Brandon McCann "zeknox" <bmccann@accuvant.com>
Thomas McCarthy "smilingraccoon" <smilingraccoon@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/netlm_downgrade.description:
This module changes the system LmCompatibilityLevel registry value
          to enable sending LM challenge hashes and initiates a SMB connection
          to the host specified in the SMBHOST module option. If an SMB server
          is listening, it will receive the NetLM hashes for the session user.
post_windows/gather/netlm_downgrade.name: Windows NetLM Downgrade Attack

author: Koen Riepe (koen.riepe <Koen Riepe (koen.riepe@fox-it.com)>
post_windows/gather/ntds_grabber.description:
This module uses a powershell script to obtain a copy of the ntds,dit SAM and SYSTEM files on a domain controller.
          It compresses all these files in a cabinet file called All.cab.
post_windows/gather/ntds_grabber.name: NTDS Grabber

author: Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
post_windows/gather/ntds_location.description:
This module will find the location of the NTDS.DIT file (from the Registry),
          check that it exists, and display its location on the screen, which is useful
          if you wish to manually acquire the file using ntdsutil or vss.
post_windows/gather/ntds_location.name: Post Windows Gather NTDS.DIT Location

actions.description: Lists all folders
actions.name: LIST

actions.description: Searches for an email
actions.name: SEARCH

author: Wesley Neelen <security@forsec.nl>
post_windows/gather/outlook.description:
This module allows reading and searching email messages from the local
          Outlook installation using PowerShell. Please note that this module is
          manipulating the victims keyboard/mouse.  If a victim is active on the target
          system, he may notice the activities of this module. Tested on Windows 8.1
          x64 with Office 2013.
post_windows/gather/outlook.name: Windows Gather Outlook Email Messages

author: Wesley Neelen <security@forsec.nl>
Matt Nelson
post_windows/gather/phish_windows_creden.description:
This module is able to perform a phishing attack on the target by popping up a loginprompt.
          When the user fills credentials in the loginprompt, the credentials will be sent to the attacker.
          The module is able to monitor for new processes and popup a loginprompt when a specific process is starting. Tested on Windows 7.
post_windows/gather/phish_windows_creden.name: Windows Gather User Credentials (phishing)

author: Garvit Dewan <d.garvit@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/psreadline_history.description: Gathers Power Shell history data from the target machine.
post_windows/gather/psreadline_history.name: Windows Gather PSReadline History

author: chao-mu
post_windows/gather/resolve_sid.description:
This module prints information about a given SID from the perspective
          of this session.
post_windows/gather/resolve_sid.name: Windows Gather Local User Account SID Lookup

author: Roni Bachar <roni.bachar.blog@gmail.com>
bannedit <bannedit@metasploit.com>
kernelsmith <kernelsmith /x40 kernelsmith /x2E com>
Adrian Kubok
DLL_Cool_J
post_windows/gather/screen_spy.description:
This module will incrementally take desktop screenshots from the host. This
          allows for screen spying which can be useful to determine if there is an active
          user on a machine, or to record the screen for later data extraction.
post_windows/gather/screen_spy.name: Windows Gather Screen Spy

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/gather/smart_hashdump.description:
This will dump local accounts from the SAM Database. If the target
          host is a Domain Controller, it will dump the Domain Account Database using the proper
          technique depending on privilege level, OS and role of the host.
post_windows/gather/smart_hashdump.name: Windows Gather Local and Domain Controller Account Password Hashes

post_windows/gather/tcpnetstat.description: This module lists current TCP sessions.

post_windows/gather/usb_history.description: This module will enumerate USB Drive history on a target host.
post_windows/gather/usb_history.name: Windows Gather USB Drive History

author: Merlyn Cousins <drforbin6@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/win_privs.description:
This module will print if UAC is enabled, and if the current account is
          ADMIN enabled. It will also print UID, foreground SESSION ID, is SYSTEM status

post_windows/gather/win_privs.name: Windows Gather Privileges Enumeration

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/gather/wmic_command.description: This module executes WMIC commands on the specified host.
post_windows/gather/wmic_command.name: Windows Gather Run WMIC Commands

author: SphaZ <cyberphaz@gmail.com>
post_windows/gather/word_unc_injector.description:
This module modifies a remote .docx file that will, upon opening, submit
          stored netNTLM credentials to a remote host. Verified to work with Microsoft
          Word 2003, 2007, 2010, and 2013. In order to get the hashes the
          auxiliary/server/capture/smb module can be used.
post_windows/gather/word_unc_injector.name: Windows Gather Microsoft Office Word UNC Path Injector

author: Joshua Abraham <jabra@rapid7.com>
post_windows/manage/add_user.description:
This module adds a user to the Domain and/or to a Domain group. It will
          check if sufficient privileges are present for certain actions and run
          getprivs for system.  If you elevated privs to system, the
          SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege will not be assigned. You need to migrate to

          exits.

author: Koen Riepe (koen.riepe <Koen Riepe (koen.riepe@fox-it.com)>
post_windows/manage/archmigrate.description:
This module checks if the meterpreter architecture is the same as the OS architecture and if it's incompatible it spawns a
          new process with the correct architecture and migrates into that process.
post_windows/manage/archmigrate.name: Architecture Migrate

author: Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
post_windows/manage/change_password.description:
This module will attempt to change the password of the targeted account.
          The typical usage is to change a newly created account's password on a
          remote host to avoid the error, 'System error 1907 has occurred,' which
          is caused when the account policy enforces a password change before the
          next login.
post_windows/manage/change_password.name: Windows Manage Change Password

author: mubix <mubix@hak5.org>
post_windows/manage/clone_proxy_settings.description:
This module copies the proxy settings from the current user to the
        targeted user SID, supports remote hosts as well if remote registry
        is allowed.
post_windows/manage/clone_proxy_settings.name: Windows Manage Proxy Setting Cloner

author: chao-mu
post_windows/manage/delete_user.description:
This module deletes a local user account from the specified server,
          or the local machine if no server is given.
post_windows/manage/delete_user.name: Windows Manage Local User Account Deletion

author: SentinelLabs
Kasif Dekel
Red Cursor
Jacob Baines
post_windows/manage/dell_memory_protect.description:
The Dell DBUtilDrv2.sys drivers version 2.5 and 2.7 have a write-what-where condition
          that allows an attacker to read and write arbitrary kernel-mode memory. This module
          installs the provided driver, enables or disables LSA protection on the provided
          PID, and then removes the driver. This would allow, for example, dumping LSASS memory
          even when secureboot is enabled or preventing antivirus from accessing the memory of
          a chosen PID.

          The affected drivers are not distributed with Metasploit. You will truly need to
          Bring Your Own (Dell) Driver.
post_windows/manage/dell_memory_protect.name: Dell DBUtilDrv2.sys Memory Protection Modifier

author: RageLtMan <rageltman@sempervictus>
post_windows/manage/download_exec.description:

post_windows/manage/download_exec.name: Windows Manage Download and/or Execute

author: Borja Merino <bmerinofe@gmail.com>
post_windows/manage/driver_loader.description: This module loads a KMD (Kernel Mode Driver) using the Windows Service API.
post_windows/manage/driver_loader.name: Windows Manage Driver Loader

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
post_windows/manage/enable_rdp.description:
This module enables the Remote Desktop Service (RDP). It provides the options to create
          an account and configure it to be a member of the Local Administrators and
          Remote Desktop Users group. It can also forward the target's port 3389/tcp.
post_windows/manage/enable_rdp.name: Windows Manage Enable Remote Desktop

author: salcho <salchoman@gmail.com>
post_windows/manage/enable_support_accou.description:
This module enables alternative access to servers and workstations
          by modifying the support account's properties. It will enable
          the account for remote access as the administrator user while
          taking advantage of some weird behavior in lusrmgr.msc. It will
          check if sufficient privileges are available for registry operations,
          otherwise it exits.
post_windows/manage/enable_support_accou.name: Windows Manage Trojanize Support Account

author: Nicholas Nam (nick <Nicholas Nam (nick@executionflow.org)>
RageLtMan <rageltman@sempervictus>
post_windows/manage/exec_powershell.description:
This module will execute a PowerShell script in a meterpreter session.

          Setting VERBOSE to true will output both the script prior to execution and the results.
post_windows/manage/exec_powershell.name: Windows PowerShell Execution Post Module

author: b4rtik
post_windows/manage/execute_dotnet_assem.description:
This module executes a .NET assembly in memory. It
          reflectively loads a dll that will host CLR, then it copies
          the assembly to be executed into memory. Credits for AMSI
          bypass to Rastamouse (@_RastaMouse)
post_windows/manage/execute_dotnet_assem.name: Execute .NET Assembly

author: Stuart Morgan <stuart.morgan@mwrinfosecurity.com>
Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>
post_windows/manage/forward_pageant.description:
This module forwards SSH agent requests from a local socket to a remote Pageant instance.
          If a target Windows machine is compromised and is running Pageant, this will allow the
          attacker to run normal OpenSSH commands (e.g. ssh-add -l) against the Pageant host which are
          tunneled through the meterpreter session. This could therefore be used to authenticate
          with a remote host using a private key which is loaded into a remote user's Pageant instance,
          without ever having knowledge of the private key itself.

          Note that this requires the PageantJacker meterpreter extension, but this will be automatically
          loaded into the remote meterpreter session by this module if it is not already loaded.
post_windows/manage/forward_pageant.name: Forward SSH Agent Requests To Remote Pageant

author: p3nt4
post_windows/manage/hashcarve.description: This module will change a local user's password directly in the registry.
post_windows/manage/hashcarve.name: Windows Local User Account Hash Carver

author: Borja Merino <bmerinofe@gmail.com>
post_windows/manage/ie_proxypac.description:
This module configures Internet Explorer to use a PAC proxy file. By using the LOCAL_PAC
          option, a PAC file will be created on the victim host. It's also possible to provide a
          remote PAC file (REMOTE_PAC option) by providing the full URL.
post_windows/manage/ie_proxypac.name: Windows Manage Proxy PAC File

post_windows/manage/inject_host.description:

post_windows/manage/inject_host.name: Windows Manage Hosts File Injection

author: Michael Long <bluesentinel@protonmail.com>
post_windows/manage/install_python.description:
This module places an embeddable Python3 distribution onto the target file system,
          granting pentesters access to a lightweight Python interpreter.
          This module does not require administrative privileges or user interaction with
          installation prompts.
post_windows/manage/install_python.name: Install Python for Windows

author: Michael Long <bluesentinel@protonmail.com>
post_windows/manage/install_ssh.description:
This module installs OpenSSH server and client for Windows using PowerShell.
          SSH on Windows can provide pentesters persistent access to a secure interactive terminal, interactive filesystem access, and port forwarding over SSH.
post_windows/manage/install_ssh.name: Install OpenSSH for Windows

post_windows/manage/make_token.description:
In its default configuration, this module creates a new network security context with the specified
          logon data (username, domain and password). Under the hood, Meterpreter's access token is cloned, and
          a new logon session is created and linked to that token. The token is then impersonated to acquire
          the new network security context. This module has no effect on local actions - only on remote ones
          (where the specified credential material will be used). This module does not validate the credentials
          specified.
post_windows/manage/make_token.name: Make Token Command

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>
phra <https://iwantmore.pizza>
post_windows/manage/migrate.description:
This module will migrate a Meterpreter session from one process
          to another. A given process PID to migrate to or the module can spawn one and
          migrate to that newly spawned process.
post_windows/manage/migrate.name: Windows Manage Process Migration

author: Scott Sutherland <scott.sutherland@netspi.com>
post_windows/manage/mssql_local_auth_byp.description:
When this module is executed, it can be used to add a sysadmin to local
          SQL Server instances.  It first attempts to gain LocalSystem privileges
          using the "getsystem" escalation methods. If those privileges are not
          sufficient to add a sysadmin, then it will migrate to the SQL Server
          service process associated with the target instance.  The sysadmin
          login is added to the local SQL Server using native SQL clients and
          stored procedures.  If no instance is specified then the first identified
          instance will be used.

          Why is this possible? By default in SQL Server 2k-2k8, LocalSystem
          is assigned syadmin privileges.  Microsoft changed the default in
          SQL Server 2012 so that LocalSystem no longer has sysadmin privileges.
          However, this can be overcome by migrating to the SQL Server process.
post_windows/manage/mssql_local_auth_byp.name: Windows Manage Local Microsoft SQL Server Authorization Bypass

author: Carlos Perez <carlos_perez@darkoperator.com>

post_windows/manage/multi_meterpreter_in.description:
This module will inject into several processes a given
          payload and connect to a given list of IP addresses.
          The module works with a given lists of IP addresses and
          process IDs if no PID is given it will start the given
          process in the advanced options and inject the selected

post_windows/manage/multi_meterpreter_in.name: Windows Manage Inject in Memory Multiple Payloads

author: Wesley McGrew <wesley@mcgrewsecurity.com>
post_windows/manage/nbd_server.description:

author: Merlyn drforbin Cousins <drforbin6@gmail.com>
post_windows/manage/persistence_exe.description:
This module will upload an executable to a remote host and make it Persistent.

author: Borja Merino <bmerinofe@gmail.com>
post_windows/manage/portproxy.description:
This module uses the PortProxy interface from netsh to set up

post_windows/manage/portproxy.name: Windows Manage Set Port Forwarding With PortProxy

author: RageLtMan <rageltman@sempervictus>
post_windows/manage/powershell/build_net.description:
This module will build a .NET source file using powershell. The compiler builds

post_windows/manage/pptp_tunnel.description:

          masquerading on the VPN server (mitm).
post_windows/manage/pptp_tunnel.name: Windows Manage Remote Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol

author: Josh Hale "sn0wfa11" <jhale85446@gmail.com>
theLightCosine <theLightCosine@metasploit.com>
post_windows/manage/priv_migrate.description:
This module will migrate a Meterpreter session based on session privileges.
          It will do everything it can to migrate, including spawning a new User level process.
          For sessions with Admin rights: It will try to migrate into a System level process in the following
          order: ANAME (if specified), services.exe, wininit.exe, svchost.exe, lsm.exe, lsass.exe, and winlogon.exe.
          If all these fail and NOFAIL is set to true, it will fall back to User level migration. For sessions with User level rights:
          It will try to migrate to a user level process, if that fails it will attempt to spawn the process
          then migrate to it. It will attempt the User level processes in the following order:
          NAME (if specified), explorer.exe, then notepad.exe.
post_windows/manage/priv_migrate.name: Windows Manage Privilege Based Process Migration

author: scriptjunkie
post_windows/manage/pxeexploit.description:
This module provides a PXE server, running a DHCP and TFTP server.
        The default configuration loads a linux kernel and initrd into memory that
        reads the hard drive; placing a payload to install metsvc, disable the
        firewall, and add a new user metasploit on any Windows partition seen,
        and add a uid 0 user with username and password metasploit to any linux
        partition seen. The windows user will have the password p@SSw0rd!123456
        (in case of complexity requirements) and will be added to the administrators
        group.

        See exploit/windows/misc/pxesploit for a version to deliver a specific payload.

        Note: the displayed IP address of a target is the address this DHCP server
        handed out, not the "normal" IP address the host uses.
post_windows/manage/pxeexploit.name: Windows Manage PXE Exploit Server

author: Ben Campbell <eat_meatballs@hotmail.co.uk>

post_windows/manage/reflective_dll_injec.description:
This module will inject a specified reflective DLL into the memory of a

post_windows/manage/remove_ca.description:

post_windows/manage/remove_ca.name: Windows Manage Certificate Authority Removal

author: vt <nick.freeman@security-assessment.com>
post_windows/manage/remove_host.description: This module allows the attacker to remove an entry from the Windows hosts file.

author: Sebastian Castro <sebastian.castro@cslcolombia.com>
post_windows/manage/rid_hijack.description:

        Taking advantage of some Windows Local Users Management integrity issues,
        this module will allow to authenticate with one known account
        credentials (like GUEST account), and access with the privileges of another
        existing account (like ADMINISTRATOR account), even if the spoofed account is
        disabled.

post_windows/manage/rpcapd_start.name: Windows Manage Remote Packet Capture Service Starter

author: Kx499
post_windows/manage/run_as.description:
This module will login with the specified username/password and execute the

author: Borja Merino <bmerinofe@gmail.com>
post_windows/manage/sdel.description:
The goal of the module is to hinder the recovery of deleted files by overwriting
          its contents.  This could be useful when you need to download some file on the victim
          machine and then delete it without leaving clues about its contents. Note that the script
          does not wipe the free disk space so temporary/sparse/encrypted/compressed files could

          could stay resident within the stream descriptor.

author: OJ Reeves
post_windows/manage/sticky_keys.description:
This module makes it possible to apply the 'sticky keys' hack to a session with appropriate
          rights. The hack provides a means to get a SYSTEM shell using UI-level interaction at an RDP
          login screen or via a UAC confirmation dialog. The module modifies the Debug registry setting
          for certain executables.

          The module options allow for this hack to be applied to:

          SETHC   (sethc.exe is invoked when SHIFT is pressed 5 times),
          UTILMAN (Utilman.exe is invoked by pressing WINDOWS+U),
          OSK     (osk.exe is invoked by pressing WINDOWS+U, then launching the on-screen keyboard), and
          DISP    (DisplaySwitch.exe is invoked by pressing WINDOWS+P).

          The hack can be added using the ADD action, and removed with the REMOVE action.

          Custom payloads and binaries can be run as part of this exploit, but must be manually uploaded
          to the target prior to running the module. By default, a SYSTEM command prompt is installed
          using the registry method if this module is run without modifying any parameters.

post_windows/manage/vmdk_mount.description:

          device and then it sends certain control code via DeviceIoControl to mount it. Use the write mode with
          extreme care. You should only open a disk file in writable mode if you know for sure that no snapshots
          or clones are linked from the file.
post_windows/manage/vmdk_mount.name: Windows Manage VMDK Mount Drive

post_windows/recon/outbound_ports.description:

          It will try to make a TCP connection to a certain public IP address (this IP
          does not need to be under your control) using different TTL incremental values.
          This way if you get an answer (ICMP TTL time exceeded packet) from a public IP
          device you can infer that the destination port is allowed. Setting STOP to

          less noise in the network).

This module send probe requests through the wlan interface.
          The ESSID field will be use to set a custom message.

author: theLightCosine <theLightCosine@metasploit.com>
post_windows/wlan/wlan_profile.description:
This module extracts saved Wireless LAN profiles. It will also try to decrypt
          the network key material. Behavior is slightly different between OS versions
          when it comes to WPA. In Windows Vista/7 we will get the passphrase. In
          Windows XP we will get the PBKDF2 derived key.
post_windows/wlan/wlan_profile.name: Windows Gather Wireless Profile
